correctness.rationale: For a source cell C, taking the event to be each whole target cell D makes its probability at every source world equal to the same minimum, proving common block masses q. Write b(P)=sum of q(D) over blocks contained in P. All rows then dominate b. For any joint choice of points, use the event complementary to the selected points: b vanishes, so a row attaining the finite minimum vanishes on the complement and must put all the mass of every positive block on its chosen point. Conversely a selector avoiding P in each positive block not wholly contained in P attains b(P). Different choices give different rows, and taking each choice once realizes the product bound whenever the source size equals the product. The displayed four-source-world example realizes it with two nontrivial target cells, while their own point-mass rows ensure commutation at those cells too. The own-cell-support corollary follows because exactly |C| distinct point masses must be realized by |C| rows.
residual_risks: The proof requires finite attainment of the lower envelope and quantifies over all Boolean events, including complements of joint choices. It does not classify infinite models or unrestricted nested expressions.
